passage:
Deepak had just put the plates on the table when Mahima said, "I need to tell you something, and I need you to let me finish." A personal loan, taken a year ago, was still owed. Mahima had been paying it quietly out of savings.

"Why didn't you tell me?" The words came out sharper than he meant. It was not the amount that stung. It was that he had been the last to know, and the past year replayed in his head, every time he had asked whether things were fine.

He breathed in and pushed his plate aside. "Okay. Show me everything: the lender, the interest, what's left."

Mahima brought the papers. By eleven they had a repayment plan on the fridge and a new rule: any debt, of any size, gets said out loud within a week.

qa.q: How long ago was the personal loan taken?
qa.a: The loan was taken a year ago.

qa.q: What is Deepak feeling as the past year replays in his head, and why?
qa.a: Hurt, mostly by the secrecy: Deepak was the last to know, and the amount was not what stung.

qa.q: What steps helped them handle the news?
qa.a: Deepak listened, asked for the full picture, and they made a repayment plan and agreed a rule to speak up about any debt within a week.

qa.q: What might it be like for Mahima to hand over the papers?
qa.a: Probably a mix of relief and nervousness, since Mahima asked to be allowed to finish speaking and then brought the papers when asked.

grounding: Mahima reveals a hidden debt; Deepak is hurt mainly by the secrecy, then listens, asks for the full picture and makes a shared plan.

passage:
Friday: Hemant found an envelope from a credit card company addressed to his wife Dilnaz, stamped "Final Reminder". He hadn't known she had that card. His stomach dropped. When she came home, he held it up. She burst into tears.
Saturday: They sat at the dining table. Hemant wanted to shout. What hurt most wasn't the amount; it was that she'd hidden it for a year. He took a breath. "I'm hurt. But tell me everything. All of it." Dilnaz explained: her brother's hospital bills, then more borrowing to cover the first. She wrote each debt on paper.
Two weeks later: They met a counsellor at the bank together and made a repayment plan. That evening, they wrote three rules on a sheet and stuck it inside the cupboard: no new credit without talking first; one money talk every month; tell the truth even when it's embarrassing. Hemant still felt a sting. But trust, he thought, could be rebuilt.

qa.q: What was stamped on the envelope?
What made Hemant feel most hurt about the hidden debt?
qa.a: He felt hurt and betrayed mainly by the secrecy, that she had hidden the card for a year, more than by the amount.

qa.q: How did Hemant and Dilnaz handle the hidden debt together?
qa.a: They listened, got the full picture on paper, made a repayment plan with a bank counsellor, and agreed honesty rules for the future.

qa.q: How might Dilnaz have felt when Hemant held up the envelope?
qa.a: Dilnaz felt ashamed and frightened, bursting into tears after hiding the debt for a year.

grounding: A partner reveals a hidden debt; the protagonist feels betrayed by the secrecy but listens, asks for the full picture, and makes a shared plan and honesty rules.

passage: Yogesh, sit. You're upset that your wife hid that loan from you. I understand. Let me tell you about me and your aunt. When I was twenty-five, a young man just married, I found out that your Kamala-mami had borrowed from a moneylender to help her sister. She hadn't told me for six months. I felt like a fool in my own house. I shouted. She cried. I slept on the veranda. The next morning, I realised I didn't know why she'd done it. So I asked, and I listened. She had been afraid I'd say no. We sat with a notebook and wrote down every rupee owed. We went to the moneylender together and agreed on a schedule. And we made a promise: no secrets about money, even the embarrassing ones. We kept it for forty years. The secret hurt more than the debt, Yogesh. Ask for the full story. That's Pradeep-mama's advice.

qa.q: How long had Kamala-mami hidden the loan?
What was Pradeep feeling when he found out about the loan?
qa.a: He felt betrayed and foolish, shouting and sleeping on the veranda.

qa.q: What turning point in the story helped Pradeep and Kamala-mami rebuild trust?
qa.a: Asking why she did it and listening, then writing every debt down, agreeing a schedule together, and making a no-secrets promise.

qa.q: How might Kamala-mami have felt while hiding the loan?
qa.a: She was probably afraid and anxious that Pradeep would refuse, which is why she kept it secret.

grounding: An elder recalls a partner's hidden debt, the hurt of secrecy, and rebuilding trust by listening, getting the full picture and agreeing honesty rules.
